system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: Nora Blake launched Remote Desktop from WS-NBLAKE-01 to FILE-NWD-01, and the server recorded a successful interactive logon (LogonType 10) from that workstation.
Nora Blake later launched Remote Desktop to DC-NWD-01, and the domain controller recorded a successful interactive logon from WS-NBLAKE-01.

The two RDP sessions are inconsistent with the supplied practice that remote administration is done only from WS-SOKAFOR-01; the records establish the connections and logons, but do not establish their purpose or actions.
Dropbox, which the supplied inventory does not list as approved, was launched under Nora's account from its installed client path.

A program named KB5034441_update.exe was launched from C:\Windows\Temp with the /quiet argument under Nora's account; the records do not establish its provenance, behavior, or whether it completed successfully.
The supplied logs show browser activity to Outlook and OneDrive, services listed as approved in the environment context.

known_telemetry_limitations: DC-NWD-01 winsec and sysmon collection was unavailable from 13:30 through 14:10 UTC because of a collection outage, overlapping the alert's reported account-creation time. The supplied sensor status identifies this gap; no record ID is provided for that status.
The supplied records do not include an account-creation event or the new account's group membership and privileges.
The RDP records establish logons, but the supplied evidence does not show what Nora did inside either remote session.
claims_not_established: The available records do not independently verify that ext.rwong was created, who created it, or when.
The available evidence does not establish whether ext.rwong was limited to the Freelancers group or was granted administrator rights.
The available evidence does not establish that the RDP sessions, Dropbox launch, or temporary update executable were malicious, or that they were connected to the reported account creation.
The available evidence does not establish whether the temporary update executable was authorized or malicious.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain domain-controller account-management and group-membership audit events for the alert window, including the actor, creation time, and privileges assigned to ext.rwong.
Review available DC and file-server records for actions performed during and after Nora's RDP sessions, and confirm whether those sessions were authorized.
Establish the provenance, signature, hash, and execution outcome of C:\Windows\Temp\KB5034441_update.exe.
Verify whether Dropbox use and the server RDP sessions were authorized by the relevant owner or a documented support request.
